raw_response:
I'm 50 this year, been farming these 13.1 mu in Quzhou County for 30 years. I finished middle school, so I can read the extension leaflets and do basic calculations, but honestly most of what I know comes from doing this every season and watching what works on my own fields. My household has six people, but my son and daughter-in-law work at a factory in town, and my daughter is only home on weekends. So day-to-day it's mainly me and my wife out here.

It's mid-April now, and the soil is warming up. I'll plant cotton around April 22nd — that's the window I trust, and my neighbors are getting their seedbeds ready too. I buy hybrid cotton seed from the county supply store; costs about 60 yuan per mu. I stopped saving my own seed years ago because the hybrids are more uniform and handle the local pests better.

For fertilizer, the extension agent at the township meeting last winter said 15–18 kg of nitrogen per mu is the "recommended" rate for high yield. But fertilizer prices went up again this spring, and after my nephew's wedding last year where I lent my brother some money, I'm tighter on cash than usual. I know my soil pretty well after three decades — it's decent loam, not great, not bad. So I'm going with 50 kg per mu of compound fertilizer (15-15-15) as a base before planting. That gives me about 7.5 kg each of N, P, and K per mu. Then I'll topdress twice with urea: about 8 kg per mu at early flowering in July, and another 7 kg per mu in early August if the bolls are setting well. Total nitrogen comes to around 14.5 kg per mu. It's a little less than what the book says, but I've done 14 kg before and still got a decent crop. I'd rather keep 800 yuan in my pocket for an emergency than push for an extra 20 kg of lint I might not get if the weather turns.

Irrigation: I have a tube well, but the electricity for pumping keeps getting more expensive. You can't skip water on cotton though — it'll abort the bolls. I'll irrigate three times: once right before planting to get good germination, once at peak flowering in mid-July, and once in mid-August when the bolls are filling. Flood irrigation, same as I've always done. I don't have drip lines, and even if I did, I can't afford to install them on just 13 mu.

For pests, cotton always has pests. I'll spray herbicide before planting to keep the weeds down. Then insecticide four times through the season — aphids early, then bollworm is the real enemy. I buy the generic brands; they cost half the name-brand stuff and work fine in my experience. If I see disease spots I might add a fungicide, but usually the insects are the bigger problem.

Tillage: I plow once with my small tractor, then harrow twice. Takes me about two days for the whole plot. In June when the wheat farmers are scrambling to plant maize, I don't have that pressure — cotton gives me a bit more time, which is one reason I stick with it.

Labor is tight. Planting, spraying, and irrigating are manageable for me and my wife. But harvest is the bottleneck — cotton has to be hand-picked, and over 13 mu that means multiple passes from September through October. If my daughter can get weekends off, we'll manage as a family. But if she's busy at the factory, I'll need to hire maybe 5 days of casual labor at 150 yuan per day. That's an expense I'd rather avoid, but leaving cotton unpicked in the field is worse.

Yield expectation: Last year I got about 290 kg of lint per mu. Two years ago was better, around 310 kg. Unless we get an early cold snap or a bad bollworm outbreak, I'm hoping for around 290 kg per mu this year. I'm not trying to break records — I just need a stable harvest to cover my costs and have something left for the family.
